author: Lucy Campbell
description:
Key states like Florida, Georgia, Michigan and North Carolina see record turnout as Americans decide the direction of Congress for remainder of Trump’s term

  • Track live results from all 50 states

As polls begin to close on election night, some early House and Senate races could indicate which way the election is trending – whether Democrats are set for the blowout they’re hoping for, or whether Republicans will defy the polls and hold onto control of Congress.

There’s a strong possibility we won’t have an idea which party will come out on top until tomorrow or later this week. But these states might provide some early signs (timings are in ET):

Kentucky (polls begin closing at 6pm)

Florida (polls begin closing at 7pm
title: US midterm elections 2026 live updates: key House and Senate races to determine control of Congress for remainder of Trump’s term

author: David Smith in Austin, Texas
description:
Results will determine makeup of Congress and other key offices and could define president’s final two years in office

  • US midterms 2026 live – latest updates

  • US midterm elections 2026: live results from Senate, House and governor races in all 50 states

Donald Trump faced a political reckoning on Tuesday as millions of Americans voted in midterm elections that could shift the balance of power in Washington and define the final two years of his divisive presidency.

Based on consistently favourable opinion polls, Democrats were optimi
title: US midterm voters poised to deliver verdict on Trump’s second term

author: José Olivares in Minneapolis
description:
Residents are sending a clear message about the violent deportations taking place across the US this midterm cycle

Minnesota voters left “I Voted” stickers on memorial sites for Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good, the two US citizens killed by federal immigration officials earlier this year.

Pretti, a 37-year-old intensive care unit nurse at the Veterans Affairs medical center in Minneapolis, Minnesota, and Good, a writer and mother of three, were killed during a large-scale immigration enforcement operation in the Minneapolis region in January.

Continue reading...
title: Minneapolis community leave ‘I Voted’ stickers at memorial sites for Alex Pretti and Renee Good

author: Johana Bhuiyan
description:
In announcement geared to schools, tech giant showed how entwined AI is with the world’s most popular website

Google just acknowledged that you can’t use Google Search without using artificial intelligence.

The search giant announced a slate of new AI products for classrooms and schools on Tuesday as well as more ways for teachers and schools to limit or restrict use of those AI tools. The company said the schools should have control over whether students use AI in the classroom. There’s one catch, though: if a school or teacher blocks the use of Google’s AI features, students won’t be able to use Google Search.

Continue reading...
title: Google says there’s no way to use Search without using artificial intelligence

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
Legal body handling identification says three latest victims include two Australians and a Japanese citizen

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Two Australians are among 69 people who died in last week’s high-speed train collision after Spanish authorities confirmed the identities of three more victims.

A legal body set up to handle the identification work, made up of police and forensics experts, announced in a statement late on Monday the three latest confirmed victims – two Australians and a Japanese citizen. They have not been named.

Continue reading...
title: Two Australians confirmed dead in Spain’s high-speed train crash

author: Maya Yang
description:
500-plus-day search for Kylie Arellano ends as FBI warns of ‘gore groups’ targeting and exploiting children

A 17-year-old girl who disappeared last year from Garden City, Utah, has been found in Oregon, and a 39-year-old man has been taken into custody.

The recovery of the teenager took place last Sunday, following a 500-plus day search involving Oregon law enforcement, the FBI’s Salt Lake City field office and the Rich county sheriff’s office in Utah.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested as girl, 17, found in Oregon after disappearing from Utah last year

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Party leader Ed Davey ‘disappointed and upset’ at decision by independent panel after claims original investigation was flawed

The Liberal Democrat peer Chris Rennard has been told there will be no further investigation into sexual harassment allegations made against him, after an independent panel concluded it could not reopen the claim.

The party leader, Ed Davey, said he was “disappointed and upset” by the conclusion, having suspended Rennard from the party after an investigation was reopened earlier this year amid claims a previous inquiry was flawed.

Continue reading...
title: Panel rules out further inquiry into sexual harassment claims against Lib Dem peer Chris Rennard

author: Associated Press
description:
Oklahoma man accused of sending letters with white nonhazardous powder before 2024 and 2026 elections

Federal authorities have charged an Oklahoma man with sending hundreds of letters containing nonhazardous white powder to public officials before the 2024 and 2026 elections.

The powders turned out to be yeast or flour, though not all letters had been fully tested, the FBI said in a court filing made public on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: US man charged with mailing hundreds of letters containing powder to officials before midterms

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
Nations in the group fare worse than others, with funding for nature projects especially hard hit even as climate crisis intensifies global need

The UK government has slashed overseas aid to Commonwealth countries, the Guardian can reveal, in contrast to the warm words for the group from King Charles and the prime minister, Andy Burnham, this week.

Amid sharp cuts in the UK’s aid budget overall, the Commonwealth has fared poorly, an analysis of the most recent and projected aid figures, seen by the Guardian, has shown.

Continue reading...
title: UK makes huge aid cuts to Commonwealth nations despite warm words at Chogm summit

author: Hannah Al-Othman North of England correspondent
description:
Nine men stand trial in Manchester accused of participating in abuse at couple’s home in Stockport, or encouraging it online

The Stockport man who drugged, raped and sexually assaulted his wife personally found a large number of the “many, many men whose fantasy is an unconscious and unresponsive woman”, a court has heard.

Nine men are on trial at Manchester Minshull Street crown court, accused of either participating in the abuse, which took place at the couple’s home, or encouraging it online.

Continue reading...
title: Man who drugged and raped wife found many men ‘whose fantasy is an unconscious woman’, court told

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Cleveland Meredith arrested after allegedly posting a call to execute all judges involved in 2021 US Capitol attack trials

A man pardoned by Donald Trump for participating in January 6 attack on the US Capitol and threatening to kill the then house speaker, Nancy Pelosi, is facing new charges for threatening to kill federal judges that presided over his and other cases arising from the violent anti-government clash.

Cleveland Meredith, from North Carolina, was arrested on Monday over a Facebook post in April that allegedly read: “ALL J6 Federal JUDGES will be EXECUTED!”

Continue reading...
title: Pardoned January 6 participant charged over alleged threats to kill federal judges

author: Adria R Walker
description:
Person arrested after fire at police department where officer who shot and killed one-year-old Kohen Wiley had worked

In the early hours of 31 October, a fire broke out at the Senatobia police department in Mississippi, which has been embroiled in controversy recently after one of its officers shot and killed Kohen Wiley, a one-year-old. Though the cause of the fire has not been reported, it is being investigated as arson by agents with the US Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives.

In June, then Senatobia police sergeant Hunter Foster shot Kohen as he sat in his mother’s arms in a Walmart parking lot. Foster, who is white, was responding to a report of an alleged shoplifting; Kohen, his mother and the driver of the vehicle, are Black.

Continue reading...
title: Officials investigate fire at Mississippi police department tied to fatal shooting of Black toddler

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Exclusive: Community and Public Sector Union denounces ‘privatisation by stealth’, joining growing number of unions turning on Carroll government

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Victoria’s public servants union says it will not support Labor at this month’s state election, condemning the government for cutting public service jobs while spending $1.2bn on consultants.

The Community and Public Sector Union (CPSU) will announce the decision on Wednesday, joining several other unions that have refused to back Labor or are actively campaigning against the govern
title: Public service union refuses to back Labor at Victorian election, condemning job cuts and $1.2bn consultant spend

author: Catie McLeod
description:
Australia’s worst products and services for the year have been named by consumer advocacy group Choice

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Concert tickets that surge to $1,650, an airline pocketing $75m of unused flight credits and a washer/dryer cycle that takes 25 hours have all made the dishonour roll in consumer advocacy group Choice’s annual Shonky awards.

Now in their 21st year, the Shonkys spotlight Australia’s worst products and services as decided by Choice.

Continue reading...
title: Ticket sellers, Virgin flight credits and a 25-hour laundry cycle: meet Choice’s 2026 Shonky award winners

author: Tess Ikonomou
description:
Annual reports show NSW renewable company’s CEO opted out of cash bonus, while CSIRO’s chief received an extra $200,000

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Executives at the troubled Snowy Hydro company collectively banked bonuses worth a combined $751,925 in the last financial year, despite its renewable energy project blowing out to 12 times its original cost.

But Guardian Australia can reveal chief executive, Dennis Barnes, who has a base salary of $1,845,126, opted not to accept the extra cash.
title: Snowy Hydro 2.0 executives awarded bonuses totalling $751,925 despite cost blowout

author: Australian Associated Press
description:
The children’s author claims he experienced trauma in childhood as he begins seven-month sentence for possessing depraved material

  • Warning: This article contains graphic content

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The disgraced best-selling author Craig Silvey has claimed he experienced trauma as a child in a 9,000-word apology published after he was jailed for child exploitation offences.

The young adult novelist was sentenced on Monday to seven months’ imprisonment, after being charged in January and subsequently pleading guilty t
title: ‘I am deeply sorry’: Craig Silvey pens 9,000-word apology for child exploitation material offences

author: Sarah Butler
description:
David Potts to take over immediately as executive chair Allan Leighton steps back to non-executive strategic role

  • Business live – latest updates

Asda has appointed David Potts, the 69-year-old former boss of Morrisons, as its chief executive with immediate effect as it continues to struggle to lift sales.

The UK’s third largest supermarket said its 73-year-old executive chair, Allan Leighton, who has been running the business since 2024, would now step back to a non-executive role focusing on “the long-term strategic agenda for the business”.
title: Asda appoints former Morrisons boss as chief executive as sales struggle

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Bodybuilding slang referring to making someone else look inferior was among entries concerning AI and climate crisis

Mogging – meaning to outperform or outshine someone or something – has been named Collins’s word of the year 2026.

Announcing the winner in an article for Collins, the copywriter Rachel Quin said the term describes making someone or something look inferior in terms of appearance, confidence or status.

Friendslop A term adopted by gamers to describe low-budget, multiplayer indie titles focused on social fun over high-end graphics.

Fricy A portmanteau of “fruity” and “spicy”, reflecting a rise in popular food products such as pineapple and mango hot sauces.

Bixie A hairstyle blending a bob and a pixie cut, recently adopted by figures such as Zendaya, Jessie Buckley, and H
title: ‘Mogging’ crowned Collins word of the year

author: Yohannes Lowe (now); Lucy Campbell (earlier)
description:
Polls open across the US where key Senate and House races will decide which party controls Congress for remainder of Donald Trump’s second term

  • Sign up for the Breaking News US email

  • What are the races to watch and why do they matter?

The US Congress has two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. Both must approve federal legislation before it can become law and both play important roles in overseeing the executive branch.

The House is elected every two years, meani
title: US midterm elections 2026 live: Americans go to the polls in referendum on Trump’s agenda

author: Lisa O’Carroll Senior correspondent
description:
Agreement to ease rules on food imports and exports is now expected to come into force in first quarter of 2028

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The EU and the UK have completed their deal to remove Brexit checks on imports and exports of food and animal products ranging from sausages and cheese to leather goods and flowers.

It will prove a boon for British food exporters, for whom trade with Europe has dropped by a third since 2019, and will also mean smaller retailers in the UK such as delicatessens can return to buying smaller batches of cheese and wines, something that became impossible because of the cost of Brexit checks introduced in 2022.
title: Deal finalised to remove Brexit checks on food and animal products

author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
description:
Australia says easing of rules has led to surge in British visitor numbers, putting pressure on local workforce

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The Australian prime minister, Anthony Albanese, has told Andy Burnham he is looking at changing rules for British backpackers in Australia, after an increase in the number of travellers visiting popular hotspots such as Sydney.

Albanese, who met Burnham on Monday evening at the Commonwealth heads of government meeting (Chogm) in the Caribbean, told reporters he wanted to discuss changing the agreement between the UK and Australia that removes a regional work requirement for British travellers.

Continue reading...
title: Australia seeks to change visa deal with UK after influx of Britons

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Parents of teenager stabbed in Southampton last year hit out at political ‘game’ played with son’s murder

Henry Nowak’s family said he “would have hated” the riots that followed his death as they accused some politicians of playing a “game” with their son’s murder.

Nowak, who was fatally stabbed by Vickrum Digwa last year, was handcuffed by police as he lay dying when his attacker falsely accused him of racial abuse.

Continue reading...
title: Henry Nowak ‘would have hated’ riots after his murder, says family

author: Melissa Davey Medical editor
description:
About 400 staff affected by closure at both Mater’s Brisbane and Springfield hospitals, with financial sustainability of pathology business a factor

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In-house pathology services at one of Queensland’s biggest hospitals will permanently close amid an investigation into potential formaldehyde exposure and continual financial strain.

The closure, which affects 400 staff across Mater’s Brisbane and Springfield hospitals, includes the lab which handles foetus and newborn tissue and cell testing for unexpected deaths.

Continu
title: Major Queensland hospital to close pathology labs amid potential formaldehyde exposure investigation

author: Caroline Davies
description:
Collection gems include 1605 Thanksgiving Act passed after Guy Fawkes’s failure and the longest act in the archives

As Bonfire Night approaches and firework displays light up the UK, in a file on a shelf in the labyrinthine National Archives can be found a flat vellum page, inscribed in exquisite calligraphy, and the origin of this week’s explosive celebrations.

The 1605 Thanksgiving Act was passed by James I after Guy Fawkes’s failure to assassinate the king, the Lords and the Commons, at the opening of parliament that year.

Continue reading...
title: Law behind Bonfire Night among records sent from parliament to National Archives

author: Tom McIlroy Political editor
description:
Labor and Coalition members sponsoring resource companies and lobby group representing online gambling giants

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Labor and Coalition MPs are facilitating permanent access to Parliament House for the country’s biggest resources companies and the lobby group representing online gambling giants, new data has revealed.

Updated rules about access passes to parliament’s private offices require MPs who sponsor lobbyists and other private interests to be disclosed on a public register. However, Tuesday’s first release of data provided very limited detail, with a backlog of more than 1,000 applications yet to be processed.
title: MPs granting powerful political lobbyists unfettered access to Australia’s parliament, data reveals

author: Kat Wong
description:
Recordings from police officer to man he’d met on dating app include one in which Lamarre-Condon states: ‘I’m in bed … not feeling the best’

Beau Lamarre-Condon said he was trying to “get back into a positive mindset” in voice notes he sent in the days after he allegedly killed two men in a Sydney terrace.

The recordings were sent to a man he had met on a dating app and played to the jury in his double murder trial on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Trying to get back into a positive mindset’: court hears voice notes Beau Lamarre-Condon sent day after alleged murders

author: Nick Visser
description:
Reserve Bank is expected to raise interest rates to an 18-year high on Tuesday, the fifth hike this year

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

NSW premier warns of risk of ‘stopping the economy dead’

The NSW premier, Chris Minns, rejected commentary from some economists that the RBA’s decision would be straightforward.

I know they’ve got a just difficult decision to make. I accept that, but we’ve got to be careful that in their efforts to slow down the economy, they don’t stop it dead.

This is an extra hit to a pay packet that many people haven’t budgeted for, are not ready for. It’s going to have a massive impact on our economy.

We work each and every day on cost of livi
title: RBA interest rates live: Reserve Bank of Australia meeting today before cash rate decision and announcement – latest news

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Police confirm arrest of 37-year-old and 14-year-old boy over alleged assault outside Torquay home on Sunday night

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A man and boy have been arrested after a One Nation volunteer was allegedly attacked with a baseball bat outside his home on Victoria’s Surf Coast.

Police on Tuesday confirmed they arrested a 37-year-old Hampton Park man and a 14-year-old boy over the incident, which occurred at a Torquay home on Sunday night.

Continue reading...
title: Man and boy arrested after One Nation volunteer allegedly attacked with baseball bat in Victoria

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Jones, a former radio broadcaster, has pleaded not guilty to 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching

The Sydney Morning Herald’s chief investigative reporter, Kate McClymont, has told a Sydney court the alleged victims of Alan Jones she interviewed received no benefit from her or the media company for telling their stories.

McClymont, whose 2023 articles led to other alleged victims coming forward, is giving evidence in the lengthy trial of the former broadcaster who is facing 21 charges of indecent assault and sexual touching against five men.

Continue reading...
title: Investigative journalist Kate McClymont gives evidence in Alan Jones indecent assault trial
